title: Nonreceipt of Newborn Vitamin K and Risk of Bleeding
summary: In a retrospective US cohort of 5,240,780 infants, recorded nonreceipt of IM vitamin K was associated with more bleeding by 6 months: 288.0 versus 185.9 per 10,000 births (adjusted RR 1.47, 95% CI 1.43–1.51). Intracranial bleeding rates were 33.0 versus 13.2 per 10,000 (adjusted RR 2.43, 95% CI 2.26–2.62). Nonreceipt rose from 3.1% in 2017 to 6.8% in 2025.
findings: Death with concurrent birth-hospitalization bleeding: adjusted RR 2.69 (95% CI 2.09–3.47); causation was not established.
shortTitle: Newborn vitamin K nonreceipt and infant bleeding
limitations: Coding and medication-record errors, missed outside-system care, and residual confounding limit inference; the composite includes bleeding unrelated to vitamin K deficiency. Home births and infants under 35 weeks were not represented.
intervention: Recorded nonreceipt of newborn IM vitamin K.
whyItMatters: Ask about birth prophylaxis when evaluating infant bleeding or possible intracranial hemorrhage; nonreceipt raises concern for vitamin K deficiency.
evidenceNotes: Freely accessible publisher methods, results, tables, and limitations reviewed. No linked correction found on the page or exact-DOI search; not proof of absence. Earlier Swedish observational findings were concordant.
